why: A poll that was in flight when OTA or Surprise Me started is still applied, or counts as a failure. A slow lamp (2 earlier timeouts) then shows a false 'Lamp not responding' banner during Surprise or OTA, which is the exact problem pausePoll exists to prevent.
A poll that has been superseded or paused still counts as a failure when it times out, so the false offline banner appears during Surprise Me or OTA, or after fewer than 3 real consecutive failures.

After the lamp comes back, tapping a preset, Surprise, Reset or a theme succeeds but 'Lamp not responding' stays up until the next poll. pullFails also stays at 2-3, so one later hiccup brings the banner straight back.
After one Surprise Me or a failed OTA, returning to the tab never refreshes right away. The user sees stale sliders for up to 5 s for the rest of the session.
After brightness is set to 0 (or MQTT OFF), the power readout keeps showing the last non-zero wattage, e.g. 12.3 W, for a lamp that is off.
When another client, MQTT/Home Assistant, Reset or a preset switches the lamp back to Fire, this page keeps highlighting the old theme and keeps the old ambient colours.
'● Update available' shows on every page load even when the firmware is current.
Within 5 s of a check, the version comparison line ('Current: x → GitHub: y') is replaced by the generic amber badge, so the user loses the version info right when deciding whether to install.
During a check the amber badge flashes in. When /checkupdate answers it overwrites the text but not the colour, so 'Current: x → GitHub: y' is left in amber (#fbbf24) instead of the normal colour.
The update badge appears in the default grey and is easy to miss, so the 'silent badge' no longer draws attention.
Every brightness input or poll flips the 'off' styling, so the page flickers between lit and dimmed while dragging and shows the wrong state at rest.
The description under every slider ('Off', 'Very dim', 'Tall flames', ...) never updates from slider moves, polls, presets or Surprise.

On Chrome/Firefox or with the keyboard, a focused contrast slider is overwritten by the poll. For example, the user adjusts with the arrow keys, pauses for more than 1 s while /setc is still queued on the single-threaded ESP, and the thumb jumps back.
A keyboard or desktop user holding focus on the brightness slider has it rewritten by a poll that lands more than 1 s after their last keypress.
The ambient glow's second colour stop takes the wrong channel, e.g. Ice theme gets a red component of 230 instead of 8, so the background glow is the wrong hue.
After any slider touch, the next poll is always thrown away, so changes made from another phone or Home Assistant appear about 5 s late.

Dragging the Sparking slider sends one HTTP request per input event (dozens per drag) to the single-threaded ESP web server. The /state poll gets delayed, the lamp steps through every intermediate value, and a slow poll can trigger false offline failures.
On a phone, the Blend slider jumps back to its old value right after the user releases it. The lamp receives /setbl?v=200, but the UI shows 50 until the next poll 5 s later.
The Cooling slider snaps back to the stale value under the user's finger on touch devices.
After the user tweaks Blend, the preset button still shows as active and the AI effect name stays on screen, although the lamp no longer matches either.
After a theme change, the UI still shows a preset (or an AI effect name) as active although the theme differs from it.
After Reset to defaults, the previously loaded preset is still highlighted as active.
Tapping Fire selects Ember and tapping Plasma selects Ice. Tapping Ice sends v=4, which the server rejects with 400 {"error":"invalid"}, so nothing changes.
Android users lose the haptic tick when any slider reaches its end stop.
No haptic feedback at the Cooling slider's minimum. The python consistency suite catches this; the behaviour suite does not.
While dragging Sparking, the number and description next to it do not change, so the user cannot see what value they are choosing.
Dragging Contrast moves the Brightness slider and label instead (contrast 0 even greys the page out as 'off'), and the Contrast label does not update. The UI then disagrees with the lamp.
Nothing changes on screen. The only effect is an 'Uncaught (in promise)' console error when the lamp is unreachable. Low severity, but observable through the unhandledrejection event.

When the ESP-side download fails right after sending 200 (lamp keeps running the old firmware and never reboots), the UI sits on 'Rebooting...' with every control disabled and polling paused for ~5 minutes instead of ~38 s.

If the lamp never comes back (bricked, rolled back onto a different IP, power cut), the page stays on 'Lamp rebooting...' with controls disabled for ~10 minutes instead of ~68 s before telling the user to refresh.

Every normal OTA (35 s flash + reboot) ends with the false 'Lamp not responding. Refresh manually.' error instead of the automatic success/reload; the 1 s interval with a 2 s abort also leaves two probes in flight at once.

Narrow: a slow /info body during download is treated as 'went offline', so later old-firmware answers can raise a premature 'Update failed'. Not reachable with the harness's instant Response bodies, and unlikely on a LAN, but not provably a no-op.
Practically none. The reload usually wins, and at worst a redundant /info probe and a second reload are scheduled. The difference shows only as extra network traffic.

After a failed OTA with the old firmware still answering, the page silently stops syncing (no /state polls ever fire, offline banner can never appear). /info keeps being hammered every 3 s and the message and button are rewritten every tick, or flip to 'Lamp not responding' later.

After one 'Up to date' check the button reads 'Check for Update' but is permanently disabled until page reload. lang.js skips relabelling a disabled chk, so a language switch also leaves it untranslated.
After a failed GitHub check (e.g. transient TLS failure) the user cannot retry without reloading the page.
One dropped /checkupdate request (WiFi blip) leaves the update button dead until reload.

After any failed OTA the 'Refresh page' button the error tells you to press is disabled and does nothing, because chk is disabled by startOTA (via the dataset path: chk is disabled when Install is clicked) and never re-enabled.

In browsers that surface the ESP's immediate connection close as a network error, the UI freezes on 'Flashing...' forever with all controls disabled and polling paused, even though the lamp updates and reboots fine.
'Reset WiFi' silently restores all fire parameters to defaults instead of clearing credentials. The lamp never enters FireLamp-Setup mode while the button claims 'Rebooting...'.
The button stays live during the reboot, so a second tap reopens the sheet and can fire a second /resetwifi at the restarting lamp.
Only at exactly uptime_s==120 with a changed version, where declaring success is arguably correct anyway. No meaningful user impact; this is a pure boundary gap.

If the lamp still answers /info for ~15 s after accepting the update (slow download start), the UI declares 'Update failed', stops watching, and then the lamp reboots into the new firmware with no automatic reload. The n>10 never-offline path also becomes dead code.
The 'Up to date ✓' confirmation flashes for 0.3 s, too short to read, so the user cannot tell the check completed.
After a successful Surprise the button label goes back to 'Thinking Ns…' within a second and keeps counting forever, even though the button is enabled.
After any Surprise error the button keeps counting up 'Thinking Ns…' with no end, while it is enabled and idle.
A Gemini answer taking 25 to 30 s is applied on the lamp, but the UI already shows 'AI timed out', keeps the old slider values and drops the effect name.

Only in a very narrow window: a response whose body finishes after the 30 s mark is reported as 'AI timed out' even though it arrived. In practice ESP replies are a single small send, so this is almost never visible.
When the lamp never answers, the user gets a generic '⚠ Error' instead of '⚠ AI timed out'.
A user who has not set a key sees '⚠ Error' instead of being told to set the API key in settings.
With an invalid Gemini key the user sees '⚠ Error' instead of '⚠ Invalid API key'.
An unparseable Gemini reply shows '⚠ Error' instead of '⚠ AI response error'.
If the user retries within 4 s of an error and the retry succeeds, the new effect name disappears a moment after it appears.
An effect name that arrives within 4 s of an error is shown in error red instead of amber.

A double tap sends two /surprise requests. The second gets 429 and shows 'Rate limit', re-enables the button and resumes polling while the first request still blocks the lamp, which can raise a false offline banner. Two elapsed counters also fight over the label.
Tapping Save with an empty field posts key= and the firmware returns 400, so the user sees 'Save failed' plus a 1.5 s disabled ✗ button instead of nothing happening.
A key pasted with a trailing space or newline is rejected by the firmware (it refuses bytes below 0x21), so the user sees 'Save failed' for a valid key.
After a successful save the API secret stays visible in the input field.
After saving a key, switching language leaves the status 'Key saved ✓' untranslated.
After one network failure the Save key button stays disabled until the page is reloaded.
fetch sends text/plain, so the ESP WebServer puts the body in arg 'plain' and server.arg('key') is empty. Every save returns 400 'Save failed', and the key can never be set.
A key containing +, & or % is mangled on the wire and either saved wrong or rejected. Real Gemini keys use only [A-Za-z0-9_-], so this is low impact.
The firmware's isWebRequest() rejects the POST, so the key is never saved and the user sees Save failed or Network error.
After choosing an action in any sheet (Install, preset Delete or Rename, Reset WiFi) the sheet stays open over the page.
Every new sheet also shows the buttons from earlier sheets, including stale actions bound to the old slot or to OTA install.
Tapping outside the action sheet no longer dismisses it.
After any sheet closes, the dim overlay stays over the whole page and blocks every tap until reload, because clicking the dim calls the same broken hideSheet.
The Cancel button in every sheet does nothing.
Values on a bucket's upper edge get the wrong description, falling back to bucket 0. For example brightness 25 and 100 both read 'Off'.

For 'ssp' the code looks up #ddp, which does not exist, so the null deref throws a TypeError inside ps(). applyState then aborts at sparking, so blend and theme are never applied, and the sparking description never updates.
Russian users see every slider description in English.
After switching language, the blend slider's description stays in the old language until the slider moves.
The highlight lands on the slot after the one the user loaded.
After the user changes the AI effect with a slider, saving to an empty slot still offers the stale AI name.
A deleted preset's empty '+' button stays highlighted as active.
If the user saves a second preset within 8 s of the first, the stale timer clears pendingSlot and the check button silently does nothing.
If the user opens another slot before the save response arrives, the wrong slot is highlighted (or none if they cancelled).
Preset names lose their 15th character even though the firmware stores 15 codepoints.
A whitespace-only name is accepted and saved as a blank-looking preset. Leading and trailing spaces also count toward the 15-character limit.
Names containing &, # or + are cut or corrupted: 'R&B' is saved as 'R'.
If the user presses Escape to cancel and then Enter (the input is still focused), the preset is saved anyway.
Escape does not close the preset-name box.
On browsers or devices where the synthetic click arrives more than 40 ms after touchend, one tap loads the preset twice.
On iOS, which sends touchmove but no touchcancel during a scroll, a swipe that starts on a preset pops the action sheet or name box mid-scroll.
On desktop, pressing a preset and dragging off it still opens the long-press sheet.
After one click, releasing any later drag over that preset reloads it.
Tapping a preset that was deleted from another device highlights it as loaded, keeps its stale name and never refreshes the list.
The loaded preset is never highlighted.
Tapping an empty '+' slot does nothing, so the user cannot save a preset with a tap.
An out-of-range import entry is sent to the lamp. The firmware rejects it with 400, so the only harm is a wasted request that briefly blocks the single-threaded web server.
A request with an invalid slot is sent to the lamp. The firmware rejects it, so this is a wasted request with no data change.
Imported presets lose their colour theme and are saved with the live theme instead.
All saves hit the single-threaded ESP32 WebServer at once, so some requests time out or are dropped and presets are missing after import.
One failed save aborts every remaining slot in the import, with no error shown.
Re-importing the same file, for example after a failed or partial import, silently does nothing.
Export downloads the live lamp state instead of the presets, so the exported file cannot be imported back.
In Firefox and Safari the download fails or saves an empty file because the blob URL is revoked before the download starts.
After page load all buttons stay unlabelled, so saved presets are invisible until some other action redraws them.
Overwriting an existing preset replaces its name with 'Preset 1' or the AI name, unless the user retypes it.
Default names are off by one ('Preset 0' for the first slot).
Enter after cancelling, or a keyboard Tab to the collapsed check button, sends a save for slot -1. The firmware rejects it.
An empty name hides the box and sends a nameless save, which the firmware either rejects or stores as an unnamed slot that still shows as '+'.
The name box stays open after saving, so a second tap re-saves the preset.
Deleting a preset fails silently (the firmware returns 400) and the preset stays.
Escape no longer closes the help modal. Keyboard users have to tab to the X button.
The help modal always says 'No key set', even when a Gemini key is stored on the lamp.
After switching language, the key status stays in the old language.
With a key stored, switching language flips the status to 'No key set'.
'Key saved' shows in red and 'No key set' in green.
Keyboard and screen-reader focus stays behind the modal overlay instead of moving into the dialog.
After choosing English, the page comes back in Russian on the next load.
The Russian choice is forgotten on reload for users whose browser locale is not ru.
The RU button is never highlighted, so neither button looks selected when Russian is active.
Screen readers pronounce Russian text with English rules and vice versa, and hyphenation and spell-check use the wrong language.
A language switch during a check wipes 'Checking...' or 'Up to date ✓' and shows 'Check for Update' on a button that is still disabled.
The update badge stays in Russian after switching to English.

why: The offline banner stays in the old language after a switch.
ul() no longer re-translates the network-error key status, so a language switch leaves it in the old language
'Key saved ✓' stays in English after switching to Russian.
For up to 1 s the busy button reads 'Surprise Me', until the 1 s ticker rewrites it. This is a brief visual glitch.
Slider value descriptions stay in the old language after a switch.
Passwords containing &, +, % or = are saved corrupted, and MQTT authentication fails.
The username is never saved (server.arg('u') is empty), so the broker rejects the login.
The save goes to a 404 route. The UI shows 'Network Error' or 'Error', and the config is never saved.
isWebRequest() rejects the request, so MQTT settings can never be saved from the UI.
The browser sends text/plain, so WebServer does not parse the form args. ip, u, p and t arrive empty and the broker config is wiped.
Every save fails with 'Network Error'.
After one network failure the Save MQTT button stays disabled until the page is reloaded.
A server-side rejection leaves the button permanently disabled.
A successful save shows 'Error' and a failed one shows 'Saved ✓'.
A double-tap sends two saves, causing two NVS writes and two initMqtt reconnects.
The username is saved as the password, so broker authentication fails.
The broker IP field shows '1883' and the port field is blank. Saving without noticing breaks the config.
The page claims a password is saved when none is, and hides it when one is.
The MQTT form is always empty, so the next save overwrites the stored config with blanks and the default topic.
The stored MQTT settings never populate the form, and the error is silently swallowed.
